mechanism_claims.claim_text: KR localizes to bacterial cells and causes visible membrane damage; support includes TMR-KR/DAPI confocal localization over 1-30 min plus SEM/TEM membrane disruption at 2 uM.

entity_scope.broader_scope: Designed SAMP family only where figures/prose explicitly generalize

limitations: Direct morphology/localization supports membrane damage but does not identify a single molecular receptor or residue-level binding site.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SAMPs induce cytoplasmic membrane depolarization and increased membrane permeability across the five tested bacterial targets, with PI/permeability and membrane-potential assays reported in Figure 7.
limitations: Assays show membrane functional disruption; they do not alone prove a pore structure or solved binding geometry.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SAMPs interact with bacterial DNA and induce SOS/cell-cycle/oxidative-stress readouts; Figure 7 reports genomic DNA binding/degradation context, cell-cycle detection, SOS gene expression, DCFH-DA ROS signal, and MDA lipid oxidation.
limitations: DNA binding and stress assays support intracellular damage but should not be reported as a single exclusive target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KR treatment changes E. coli transcriptome pathways related to ribosome/protein synthesis, amino-acid biosynthesis, membrane structure/function, and DNA-related genes, supporting a multimodal downstream response.

entity_scope.target: Escherichia coli treated with 0.2 uM KR

limitations: Transcriptome enrichment is downstream pathway evidence; it is not direct proof of a specific protein target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Designed SAMPs inhibit biofilm biomass and damage established biofilms in S. aureus and E. coli assays; KR/RK reduce crystal-violet biomass below 20% of control in source text and CLSM shows more dead bacteria after treatment.
limitations: Biofilm findings are phenotype/activity evidence and should not be promoted to a molecular antibiofilm mechanism.

caution_findings.evidence_context: The paper supports membrane damage plus intracellular/omics stress responses; it does not solve a single receptor or residue-level binding target.
